description: S3 buckets must enable server access logging unless serving as a log destination

requirements.description: An S3 bucket has no server access logging configuration and is not referenced as a log destination by any other bucket in the template.
requirements.rationale: AWS recommends enabling server access logging for security auditing and visibility. A bucket without logging configured and not serving as a log destination violates the rule.

requirements.description: An S3 bucket has server access logging configured to deliver logs to a separate destination bucket.
requirements.rationale: This is the recommended configuration: logging is enabled and logs are delivered to a distinct destination bucket per AWS best practices.

requirements.description: An S3 bucket has server access logging configured to deliver logs to itself (self-logging).
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision: logging is technically enabled, satisfying the literal rule wording. AWS discourages self-logging due to infinite loop concerns, but the rule's scope is whether logging is enabled, not its quality.

requirements.description: An S3 bucket has no logging configuration of its own but is explicitly referenced as the log destination by another bucket in the template.
requirements.rationale: Log destination buckets are intentionally exempt: enabling access logging on them would create recursive log entries. Exemption requires an explicit reference from another bucket as its log target.

requirements.description: An S3 bucket has no logging configuration but appears intended as a log destination (e.g., by name or by a bucket policy granting the S3 logging service principal write access), without any other bucket in the template explicitly referencing it as a target.
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision: exemption applies only when another bucket explicitly references this bucket as its log target. Naming heuristics or policy hints are not sufficient evidence of intent.

requirements.description: An S3 bucket has no logging configuration of its own and is referenced as a log destination by another bucket whose own logging configuration is unresolvable at analysis time.
requirements.rationale: Per resolved decision: when the referencing bucket's logging cannot be confirmed, apply the destination exemption to avoid false positives.

requirements.description: An S3 bucket's logging configuration depends entirely on an unresolvable condition such that whether logging is enabled cannot be determined.
requirements.rationale: When the rule cannot definitively assert non-compliance because the configuration value is not resolvable at analysis time, it should not flag.

requirements.description: An S3 bucket has a logging configuration block present but it contains no destination bucket value (empty configuration).
requirements.rationale: An empty logging configuration does not actually enable log delivery; effectively logging is not configured and the bucket is not exempted.

requirements.description: An S3 bucket has server access logging configured with a destination bucket and an additional log file prefix.
requirements.rationale: Logging is enabled and delivered to a distinct destination; optional prefix configuration does not affect compliance.

requirements.description: An S3 bucket is referenced as a log destination by multiple other buckets in the template and has no logging configuration of its own.
requirements.rationale: Being an explicit log destination for one or more other buckets qualifies for the exemption regardless of how many source buckets target it.
